drafts.neutral_framing: Should Brevard County’s lagoon program fund a living-filter pilot every year at a city stormwater outfall, with water tests before and after?
drafts.final_wording: Storm drains in every Brevard city empty toward the Indian River Lagoon. Should the county’s lagoon program fund one living-filter pilot a year — an oyster reef, a living shoreline, or a nitrogen-removing filter bed — at a city outfall, and publish the water tests before and after?
drafts.final_wording_note: Framed around how the program spends money it already has. It does not ask about the November 3 lagoon tax renewal, which is an active ballot measure.
shaping_notes: A question about a method, not about any person, candidate, or ballot measure. The sales-tax renewal is deliberately left out; this question stands whether it passes or not.
Grounded in the county’s own BAM filter results and Brevard Zoo’s oyster reefs.
drafts.tier_note: Open as a Tier 0 sentiment poll: no account, one voice per browser, changeable until close. Tier 0 is displayed but never cited as verified resident opinion — verification tiers arrive with the full voting layer.
drafts.background: Nitrogen and phosphorus washing off streets feed the algae blooms that killed the lagoon’s seagrass and, from 2020 to 2022, starved 1,255 manatees. The county’s lagoon program already builds BAM filters; one at Broadway Pond removes about 456 pounds of nitrogen a year. See Our water.

founding_solutions.title: One living-filter pilot a year, results published
founding_solutions.summary: Each year, the lagoon program pairs one city stormwater outfall with a filter — BAM, an oyster reef, or a living shoreline — and publishes nitrogen and phosphorus tests before and after.

drafts.neutral_framing: Should the Brevard County jail’s farm and kitchen work count toward a college certificate people can finish after release?
drafts.final_wording: The Sheriff’s Farm already grows food for the Brevard County jail, and the jail already offers trade certificates. Should the Sheriff and Eastern Florida State College pilot a short farm-and-kitchen certificate that people can start inside and finish after release?
drafts.final_wording_note: Framed around two programs that already exist. Taking part would be offered, never required.
shaping_notes: A question about a program design — not about any person, candidate, or ballot measure.
Grounded in the Sheriff’s own program list and budget.

drafts.background: The Brevard County jail holds over 1,600 people a day; in February 2023, 86.8% had not been convicted. The Sheriff asked for $61.5 million to run it in FY2025-26. It already offers GED classes, ServSafe and OSHA certificates, barbering, and the Sheriff’s Farm. See Jails & prisons.

founding_solutions.title: A farm-and-kitchen certificate with Eastern Florida State College
founding_solutions.summary: Pair the Sheriff’s Farm and the jail kitchen with a short college certificate in horticulture or food safety, offered to anyone eligible who wants it, and track who finishes, who gets hired, and who comes back.

drafts.neutral_framing: Should Brevard County post every budget at the same level of detail — including the elected officers’ budgets — as downloadable data?
drafts.final_wording: Brevard posts line-item budget spreadsheets for its departments, but none for the Sheriff, Clerk, Tax Collector, Property Appraiser or Supervisor of Elections. Should every county office post its line-item budget the same way?
drafts.final_wording_note: Framed around a step each office can take on its own: publishing records it already keeps.
shaping_notes: A question about disclosure format — not about any person, candidate, or ballot measure.
Grounded in what was and was not found: 32 department spreadsheets are posted; the Charter Officers section has none (Docket #2).

drafts.background: The county’s line-item spreadsheets itemize $2.13 billion of its $2.43 billion adopted budget. The rest — about $299 million — is mostly the elected officers’ budgets, which aren’t posted in the same form (Docket #2). Not posted means not found yet, not hidden.

founding_solutions.title: Post the officers’ line items next to the departments’
founding_solutions.summary: Each elected officer posts its adopted line-item budget as a spreadsheet on the Budget Office’s Line Item Budget page, in the same format the departments use.
